title: Tensor-parameter composition under an adjunction with a tensor comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], each equipped with a tensor bifunctor $\otimes$ (it assigns an object $X\otimes Y$ to each pair of objects and a morphism $f\otimes g$ to each pair of morphisms, preserving identities and componentwise composition); no associator, unitor, symmetry or coherence condition is assumed. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be functors, and let $\mu_{X,Y}:FX\otimes FY\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X\otimes Y)$ be isomorphisms natural in $X,Y$, that is $F(f\otimes g)\circ\mu_{X,Y}=\mu_{X',Y'}\circ(Ff\otimes Fg)$. Let $F\dashv G$ have natural Hom bijections $\Phi_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,GY)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FX,Y)$, unit $u$ and counit $e$, normalized by $\Phi(h)=e_Y\circ F(h)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. For $S\in\mathcal C$ and $N\in\mathcal D$, define
$$\lambda_{S,N}:S\otimes GN\longrightarrow G(FS\otimes N)$$
to be the unique map whose $\Phi$-image is $(1_{FS}\otimes e_N)\circ\mu_{S,GN}^{-1}$. For objects $S,T,P\in\mathcal C$, $N,N'\in\mathcal D$ and maps $f:T\otimes P\to GN$, $g:FS\otimes N\to N'$, set
$$f^\sharp=e_N\circ F(f)\circ\mu_{T,P}:FT\otimes FP\to N.$$
Then
$$\Phi_{S\otimes(T\otimes P),N'}\bigl(G(g)\circ\lambda_{S,N}\circ(1_S\otimes f)\bigr)\circ\mu_{S,T\otimes P}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes\mu_{T,P})=g\circ(1_{FS}\otimes f^\sharp).$$
Both sides have source $FS\otimes(FT\otimes FP)$ and target $N'$. This is transport of tensor-parameter composition through the specified adjunction; it requires neither invertibility of $\lambda$, nor closedness or dualizability of the objects, nor any associativity or unit coherence. In particular it applies to a strong monoidal $F$ between monoidal categories.

proof.text:
Put $A=T\otimes P$, $B=FS\otimes N$ and $q=1_S\otimes f:S\otimes A\to S\otimes GN$. The Hom bijection makes $\lambda_{S,N}=\Phi^{-1}_{S\otimes GN,B}((1_{FS}\otimes e_N)\circ\mu_{S,GN}^{-1})$ well-defined and unique. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], the counit is natural and $\Phi(h)=e\circ F(h)$. Consequently, expanding the composite, preserving composition under $F$, and using $e_{N'}\circ FG(g)=g\circ e_B$ gives
$$\Phi_{S\otimes A,N'}(G(g)\circ\lambda_{S,N}\circ q)=g\circ e_B\circ F(\lambda_{S,N})\circ F(q)=g\circ\Phi_{S\otimes GN,B}(\lambda_{S,N})\circ F(q).$$
Here $g:B\to N'$ is exactly a morphism of $\mathcal D$, so counit naturality applies with no additional hypotheses.

proof.text:
Naturality of the given $\mu$ at $(1_S,f):(S,A)\to(S,GN)$, together with $F(1_S)=1_{FS}$, reads
$$F(q)\circ\mu_{S,A}=\mu_{S,GN}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes F(f)).$$
Postcompose this equality with $\mu_{S,GN}^{-1}$ and cancel $\mu_{S,GN}^{-1}\circ\mu_{S,GN}=1$. Substitute the defining $\Phi$-image of $\lambda$ from step 1. Associativity and identity laws of [def-nagata-category] give
$$\Phi_{S\otimes A,N'}(G(g)\circ\lambda_{S,N}\circ q)\circ\mu_{S,A}=g\circ(1_{FS}\otimes e_N)\circ(1_{FS}\otimes F(f)).$$
Only the specified naturality and invertibility of $\mu_{S,GN}$ have been used.

proof.text:
Precompose the equality of step 2 with $1_{FS}\otimes\mu_{T,P}$. Since the tensor bifunctor preserves componentwise composition and identities, the right side becomes
$$g\circ(1_{FS}\otimes e_N)\circ(1_{FS}\otimes F(f))\circ(1_{FS}\otimes\mu_{T,P})=g\circ\bigl(1_{FS}\otimes(e_N\circ F(f)\circ\mu_{T,P})\bigr)=g\circ(1_{FS}\otimes f^\sharp).$$
Substitute $A=T\otimes P$ and $q=1_S\otimes f$ on the left. This is the required equality. Its source is $FS\otimes(FT\otimes FP)$ throughout and its target is $N'$. No parentheses have been changed, so no associator, symmetry, unitor or coherence is used; no inverse of $\lambda$ is used.
